To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a variety of new 5′-ester derivatives of cytarabines are immunosuppressive, have antiviral activity and are antitumor agents.
a series of cytarabines were prepared in which the 5′ position of the molecule was modified with an ester group.
a variety of cytarabines with long-acting properties are effective immunosuppressive, antiherpes simplex, and antitumor agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of more effective immunosuppressive, and antiviral and/or antitumor agents.
the development of new, potent, long-acting immunosuppressive, antimicrobial, antiviral, and antitumor agents.

the synthesis and evaluation of a variety of cytarabines, with emphasis on derivatives which have the ability to exert their inhibitory effects over long periods of time, and which are resistant to enzymatic inactivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the enhanced activity of these new derivatives is due to a combination of factors: the increased resistance to deamination (inactivation) of the insoluble derivatives, the prolonged circulation times of the derivatives, the prolonged half-lives of cytarabines, and the prolonged inhibition of DNA synthesis.
the 5′ derivatives of cytarabines are potent and effective immunosuppressants and antitumor and antiviral agents.
the new 5′-derivatives of cytarabines are more potent and more convenient for clinical use than the parent compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

these new derivatives are as active as cytarabine and its congeners in inhibiting immune responses and antiviral and tumor activities, and that these activities may be achieved with simple injection schedules.
a number of cytarabines with 5′-ester groups have been found which have good immunosuppressants and antitumor activity in animals and man.
the 5′ acylated cytarabine analogs are more active than cytarabine in suppressing immune responses, inhibiting DNA synthesis, and inhibiting tumor cell growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5′ derivatives of cytarabines are more potent immunosuppressive agents than the parent nucleoside.
we can use these derivatives as a model for the study of the pharmacokinetics of drugs.
